watch_items.text: **NH general election fundraising reports (next FEC filing deadline)** — first real signal of whether Pappas-Sununu and Shaheen-DiLorenzo are drawing national money at the pace their "pivotal race" framing implies.

**Smithsonian leadership transition timeline** — watch for the White House's stated rationale for the historical-presentation review to surface, and who is named as Bunch's successor; that appointment will show how far the administration intends to push.

**Any official ABC statement on Kimmel** — the current story rests entirely on one unnamed source; a real confirmation or denial in the next 72 hours will resolve whether this was accurate reporting or a false trend claim.

**UK/Europe Israel sanctions follow-through** — whether the administration issues any statement (support, opposition, or continued silence) in response to allied moves; the current non-opposition posture is the most likely source of a real rift with the pro-Israel base if it hardens.

**Iran tanker strike aftermath** — any Iranian response, retaliation, or shipping-lane disruption in the Gulf; also watch whether right-leaning outlets pick the story up at all once the NH primary cycle clears, which would confirm this was crowding-out rather than deliberate avoidance.

**Campaign Nucleus data-collection probe** — whether any Democratic member of Congress formally requests an investigation or FEC complaint; this is the most substantively serious of the minor stories if it advances.

top_cluster.headline: New Hampshire held primaries for its open U.S. Senate seat and 1st Congressional District House seat; Chris Pappas (D) will face John E. Sununu (R) for Senate, and Anthony DiLorenzo (R, Trump-endorsed) will face Stefany Shaheen (D) for the House seat, in races viewed as pivotal to control of Congress in the 2026 midterms.
top_cluster.left_framing: Emphasizes Democratic establishment strength and a path to flipping the Senate, casts Trump-aligned Republicans as compromised or ethically troubled (aide cash gifts, redistricting maneuvering, election-data requests), and treats Trump's midterm convention and trade actions skeptically as risky, chaotic, or self-serving.
top_cluster.center_framing: Largely horse-race and procedural: treats the primary outcomes as straightforward electoral results and forecaster-driven matchups (Pappas-Sununu, Ayotte-Warmington), notes the Dallas convention and trade war as strategically significant without strongly editorializing on motive.
top_cluster.right_framing: Emphasizes Trump's continued influence over the GOP base (DiLorenzo's win as validation of his endorsement), frames Democratic primaries through an establishment-vs-socialist lens to highlight party vulnerability, and pairs NH coverage with favorable economic narratives (manufacturing rebound, business formation, bond market) as midterm tailwinds for Republicans.
top_cluster.left_omissions: Left coverage omits or downplays the positive economic narratives (manufacturing/jobs boost, business-formation records, bond market performance) that right-leaning outlets use to argue Republicans have midterm momentum, and does not frame DiLorenzo's win as evidence of Trump's continued endorsement power.
top_cluster.right_omissions: Right coverage omits Trump's $45,000-$155,000 cash gifts to White House aides, the appeals court ruling blocking IRS-ICE taxpayer data sharing, and the Missouri redistricting fight being cast as a Trump-backed gerrymander attempt — all prominent in left and center-left coverage.

blindspot_narrative: Left-leaning outlets are avoiding scrutiny of intra-Democratic dysfunction (Fetterman's censure) and are the sole source on the Iran tanker strikes, effectively controlling how (or whether) that escalation gets framed. Right-leaning outlets are avoiding Trump's disputed 9/11 self-mythologizing entirely rather than contesting it, and are alone in flagging discomfort with the administration's non-opposition to UK/Europe Israel sanctions — both patterns suggest each side is shielding its own principals from a symbolically loaded week (9/11 anniversary, midterm-defining primaries) while amplifying the other's internal disorder rather than external policy actions.
